submission.justification:
Crystal-K1 at 4 cm gives the best simulated energy resolution at 662 keV (FWHM 2.893%, simulation only, 100k events). K1 is best at every thickness tested. The 4 cm value is statistically tied with 6 cm (2.872%), and I chose 4 cm because a smaller crystal volume generally means less intrinsic activity. That choice is my judgement, not a simulation result. The 3.5 to 6 cm range is a plateau near 2.9%, and resolution degrades at 10 cm for all crystals.

The low-background suitability constraint is NOT verified. No project document gives radiopurity limits, intrinsic U/Th/K-40 or Cs-137 activity, or a facility background requirement for K1, K2 or K3. The recommendation is therefore conditional. K1 must pass a radiopurity screen (measured or vendor-supplied intrinsic activity) before procurement is finalised. If K1 fails, the fallback is Crystal-K2 at about 5 cm (FWHM 4.45%). All results are simulation-only and have not been validated against measurement.

[s4 summary] Crystal-K1 at about 4 cm is my recommendation for resolution, but it is not yet cleared for low-background use, because no project document gives radiopurity limits or intrinsic activity data for any of the three crystals.

**Refinement of Crystal-K1 (100k events per run, FWHM at 662 keV):**

| Thickness | FWHM (%) |
|---|---|
| 3.5 cm | 2.884 |
| 4 cm | 2.893 |
| 5 cm | 3.031 (from earlier scan) |
| 6 cm | 2.872 |
| 6.5 cm | 3.075 |

The 3.5–6 cm region is a plateau near 2.9%. The 5 cm value sits above both neighbours, so run-to-run scatter is probably about 0.1% absolute. The best sampled point is 6 cm (2.872%), but 4 cm (2.893%) is statistically tied. I chose 4 cm because a smaller crystal volume generally means less intrinsic activity for low-background work. That choice is my judgement, not something the simulation determines.

**Low-background comparison:** None of the project documents contains radiopurity limits, intrinsic U/Th/K-40 or Cs-137 activity data, or a facility background requirement. So K1, K2 and K3 all remain unverified against the low-background constraint. K1 is recommended on resolution alone, conditional on passing a radiopurity screen (measured or vendor-supplied intrinsic activity) before procurement is finalised.

**Trade-offs and caveats:**
- K1 is about 2.9% at its optimum, against about 4.4% for K2 and about 9.0% for K3. Its radioactivity is unknown, which is the main risk to this choice.
- At 10 cm, resolution degrades for all three crystals, so the earlier "weak thickness dependence" note holds only roughly between 3 and 8 cm.
- All results are simulation-only and have not been checked against measurement.
- Fallback if K1 fails the radiopurity screen: K2 at about 5 cm (4.45%).

I recorded the results, the chosen crystal (K1) and thickness (4 cm), and these caveats with `record_results`.
